cause_found_in_code: PostgresIncidentStore._refresh_from_disk ran list_all() on BOTH tables and parsed every row into dataclasses; it is called by every read method, so one GET /api/incidents?open_only=true cost two full-table loads (more with the stale-finding probe), each materialising all cases and postmortems.
/health metrics used len(store.list_incidents()), a full load per scrape.
consume-agent-finding counted ids with list_incidents(); infrastructure recovery fallback iterated list_incidents(); retired-binding resolve iterated list_incidents().
Startup built the same full cache, and a deploy-restart burst of degradation/recovery calls repeated the full reload per call.

fix.store: PostgresIncidentStore keeps only open/investigating cases resident (status IN predicate); point reads by record_id for any other case; postmortems never preloaded (keyed by postmortem_id or incident_id); query_incidents filters in SQL with ORDER BY/LIMIT; count_incidents/count_incidents_with_id_prefix use SELECT count(*); list_postmortems and by-binding/pool reads capped at 1000 rows; infra alias and latest-component lookups restricted to infra bindings with LIMIT.
fix.routes: GET /api/incidents uses store.query_incidents with new optional limit; default page 1000 unless open_only (bounded by open set). /health uses count_incidents. Consumer/agent-finding/retired-binding paths use the bounded store methods.
fix.owner_store: PostgresJsonOwnerStore.select_where and count_where added (trusted SQL, parameterised values).
fix.compose: DEV_MEM_LIMIT_INCIDENTS unchanged (2g); no peak was measured, so no change is justified
